sources.title: 37.106.601, Minimum Standards for a Skilled and Skilled/Intermediate Care Facility: General Requirements
sources.notes: rules.mt.gov (the Esper policy-library platform) serves only a client-side application shell to curl -- confirmed 2026-09-12, HTTP 200 but zero rule-number occurrences in the raw response, no __NEXT_DATA__ or other JSON island. The standing packet's own URL (a /search?query= address) is a search results page, not a fetchable document; the rule text lives at this permalink, found via the site's own search and confirmed to render the requested rule. The trailing path segment (8d6002f2-...) is this platform's own rule-version identifier -- an application-level UUID per PROVENANCE.md's API-source rule -- and can change if the site is redeployed or the rule is re-versioned; a broken link here is capture drift to re-establish via the site's search, never evidence the rule was withdrawn. Read with the browser tool's get_page_text (raw visible text, not an AI summary) and supplied with extractor none because the reader has already flattened the page -- same convention as Florida. Verified byte-identical across two independent navigations 2026-09-12. Supplied text is trimmed of the global site footer (Home | Contact Us | ADA Notice & Accommodations | Accessibility | Privacy & Security | Disclaimer | Support | Powered by), which is common to every page on the site and carries no rule content, matching how the standing packet was trimmed.

sources.title: 37.40.338, Bed Hold Payments
sources.notes: Located via rules.mt.gov's own search for 'bed hold' (first result, exact title match, of 1000 loosely-ranked hits) while deepening the state's baseline page, which had recorded any DPHHS Medicaid bed-hold provision as pending. Same platform and same reasoning as sources 2-4: rules.mt.gov serves no rule text to curl (confirmed 2026-09-26, HTTP 200 but an empty application shell); the trailing UUID is an application-level identifier per PROVENANCE.md, not a stable citation, and a broken link is capture drift to re-establish via the site's search, not evidence of withdrawal. Read with get_page_text, extractor none, verified byte-identical across two independent navigations 2026-09-26. Global site footer trimmed from the supplied text, as with sources 2-4. The rule states no fixed day count for a hospital-absence bed-hold at all -- payment continues only while the facility is full with a waiting list and the department has given written approval, with no outer day limit stated -- and a separate, explicit cap (72 consecutive hours per absence, 24 days per rate year) for therapeutic home visits, a different kind of absence from hospitalization. This is Montana's Medicaid bed-hold policy as published, not a hospitalization day-count comparable to the fixed figures other states publish.
